sources.entry: Contao - Powerful CMS that allows you to create professional websites and scalable web applications. (Demo, Source Code) LGPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Contao is an open source PHP content management system for building professional websites and scalable web applications, and this repository is the monorepo used to develop its bundles.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is a development monorepo that holds the source for the Contao CMS bundles, including ApiBundle, CalendarBundle, CommentsBundle, CoreBundle, FaqBundle, ListingBundle, MakerBundle, ManagerBundle, McpBundle, NewsBundle, NewsletterBundle and OauthServerBundle. The README says these are split automatically into separate packages. It is meant for contributors who want to open pull requests or report issues, and it states that the monorepo itself should not be used in production. The README describes a workflow that installs the Contao Managed Edition with Composer, points its require section at the monorepo, and makes changes in vendor/contao/contao that can be committed from the application. It also documents running code quality tools (rector, ECS, PHPStan, unit, functional and end-to-end tests) through Composer scripts, and building frontend assets with Node.js.
use_cases: contributing a pull request to Contao
reporting an issue in a Contao bundle
developing Contao bundles locally inside a Managed Edition install
running Contao's test suites and code quality checks
building a professional website with a PHP CMS
how_to_run: Adjust the require section of composer.json to use contao/contao with dev-main (or .x-dev for bug fixes)
composer bin all install (inside vendor/contao/contao, for code quality tools)
npm ci && npm run build (Node.js 18.12 or newer)
notable: Monorepo that is automatically split into separate Contao bundle packages
Clones the monorepo into vendor/contao/contao so changes can be submitted as pull requests from a running application
Composer scripts cover rector, ECS, PHPStan, unit, functional and end-to-end tests
End-to-end suite builds an isolated Managed Edition with Docker-supplied MariaDB and Playwright browser tests
caveats: The README says not to use contao/contao in production; use the split bundle packages instead
Development setup requires PHP 8.4, Composer, and Node.js; browser tests need Node.js 20 or newer
Functional tests need a manually created database and an edited phpunit.xml
